1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.
2. The applicant seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.0537 of 2021, under Section 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Kotwali Mohammadi, District Lakhimpur Kheri.

3. In terms of the FIR it was alleged that the daughter of the informant was married on 26.04.2016 and sufficient dowry was also given, however, the matrimonial family used to demand dowry and on Rajnish Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl .Chief Secy.

1 12.06.2021, she was killed by demonstrating some poison to him.
4.

Contention of learned counsel for the applicant is that the the allegations have been levelled against the entire family members with regard to demand of dowry without there being anything specific that soon before her death, the victim was subjected to any physical or mental cruelty in relation to demand of dowry.
The cause of death as per the FSL is Organophosphorus Insecticide.

He, thus, argues that it was a case of suicide as the deceased was unwell.
5.
Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the allegations levelled in the FIR being general in nature without there being anything specific against the husband with regard to harassment soon before her death coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal history and is in custody since 12.04.2022, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Rajnish Kumar be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
